subject: Urgent: Forensic snapshot request + SOC 2 control matrix clarification
messages:
From: Tara Singh <security@finbridge.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Lurie <alex.lurie@finbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Suspicious API usage — request for snapshot and SOC 2 control matrix

Hi Irene,

We found anomalous activity in our logs that looks like unusual token usage against the Redwood inference API tied to a handful of customer IDs. We do not yet believe there was exfiltration of customer data, but our security and compliance team needs a short forensic snapshot to triage. Specifically, can you provide the following by EOD PT tomorrow (31 May):

- A forensic snapshot (zipped) with request/response headers for 2027-05-28 -> 2027-05-30 for the affected client IDs (sample CSV included).
- A mapping or SOC 2 control matrix indicating where Redwood documents alerting, logging, and evidence retention for inference requests (we're looking for control IDs for audit purposes).
- Any immediate mitigations taken (IP blocks, credential rotation, customer notifications).

I've attached a short request form and a CSV sample of the API request IDs we correlate with the anomaly (attachment: suspicious-api-usage-sample.csv). We can share more context over a quick call if helpful.

Please cc your incident lead and compliance reviewer on the response. Our deadline is tight because we have a quarterly audit in two weeks.

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Head of Security Operations
FinBridge

Attachments: forensic_request_form.pdf, suspicious-api-usage-sample.csv

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <security@finbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alex Lurie <alex.lurie@finbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious API usage — request for snapshot and SOC 2 control matrix

Tara — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. We will prioritize. Quick summary of next steps from our side:

1) Forensic snapshot: we'll produce a curated forensic snapshot (redacted where required) containing request/response headers, request IDs, and matching access logs for 2027-05-28 -> 2027-05-30. Our security engineer will package the snapshot as a password-protected zip and deliver a download link.

2) SOC 2 control mapping: we'll export the SOC 2 control matrix tying our logging/monitoring/incident detection controls to the documentation and control IDs you referenced. Expect a PDF (highlighting controls that cover S3/API logging, alerting, and retention).

3) Mitigations: we have temporarily rotated the service token associated with the impacted API key, and added a short-lived IP denylist for the suspicious sources while we complete triage. No customer-facing notifications have been sent yet — we'll coordinate on language if required.

Logistics:
- ETA for initial package: 2027-05-31 14:00 PT (we will alert you earlier if readiness slips).
- Point of contact: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com) is the incident investigator; Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwood.com) will own the SOC 2/control matrix export.

Can you confirm the list of affected customer IDs you want included (the CSV sample you sent looks like a subset)? Also confirm whether FinBridge wants the full set of headers for each request or just a filtered set (we typically redact Authorization and include a hash of the token).

Appreciate the tight window — we'll aim to get the snapshot and control mapping published to a secure Drive folder with a one-time link.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-irp-v2.pdf (internal control/runbook), forensic_snapshot_20270530.zip (to-be-delivered)

From: Tara Singh <security@finbridge.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Lurie <alex.lurie@finbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 12:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious API usage — request for snapshot and SOC 2 control matrix

Irene, thanks for the rapid reply.

We confirm the CSV attached earlier (request-ids.csv) is the full set for our scope — sorry for not flagging earlier. For the headers, full request/response headers are preferred if you can provide them in a redacted bundle (we need to validate any anomalous request parameters). If redaction of Authorization is standard for you, that's fine so long as you include a stable token hash.

One additional ask: please include a sample of your runtime telemetry around those request IDs (latency, model, sequence length) if available — it helps our triage.

We are available for a 20-minute sync this afternoon if you think it helps.

Thanks,
Tara
